turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Mr. Hale. Thank you for seeing me. I have twenty minutes.

Owen has a zero. Fifteen percent of his English mark. You entered it before you called me.

Walk me through it. What exactly did you see, and when?
I don't think this is productive.

Then let's make it productive. I'll start.

I'm not here to argue about Owen's character. I'm here about a process.

A zero went into the gradebook. A call to me came after. That order matters.

So, one question. What is the date you ran the essay through the checker, and which tool was it?
I'm going to go. I have a class in ten minutes.

Ten minutes is fine. I'll take them.

Before you go, two things. Nothing is said to Owen's class. Not today, not about him.

And I'd like the checker's name and the date you ran it, in an email, by end of day tomorrow. Plus the report itself.

That's all I'm asking right now. Can you do that?
Email the principal if you want. I'm done here.

Understood. I will email the principal.

I'll copy you, so nothing in it surprises you.

One thing first, and I'm asking, not arguing. Owen's name doesn't come up in front of that class. Can I have your word on that?
